messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  (none)

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  (none)

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Rajesh Patel had lived with the echoes of war for over six decades. As he approached his 80th birthday, the memories that once seemed to fade like scars on a weathered palm now pulsed with an otherworldly vitality. A veteran of India's 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War, Rajesh's time in combat was a crucible that had shaped him in ways both visible and invisible. His days were spent working as a warehouse worker, surrounded by the hum of machinery and the gentle clang of shelving units being stocked and restocked. The rhythmic din was comforting, almost soothing – a reminder that some patterns remained constant despite life's turbulence. Yet, amidst this familiarity, Rajesh found himself increasingly disconnected from the world around him. His coworkers would sometimes catch him staring off into space, lost in thought as his mind wandered back to those war-torn days. Rajesh's relationship with his family had grown strained over the years. His divorce several decades ago still lingered like an open wound. He couldn't help but wonder if things might have turned out differently had he been able to shake off the ghosts of '71. Despite this, his children and grandchildren remained a source of comfort – though he struggled to express emotions that felt buried beneath layers of accumulated pain. Rajesh's nights were filled with an unsettling quiet. His apartment seemed larger than it needed to be, echoing with the silences that only a solitary life could bring. He'd often find himself lying awake, replaying memories that refused to be extinguished – memories he'd long ago resigned himself to carrying like so much emotional baggage. As Rajesh navigated his twilight years, he began to feel an unshakeable sense of disconnection from the world around him. His body ached in ways both familiar and new, yet it was the ache within that felt most oppressive. The life he'd built – imperfect as it was – now seemed precariously balanced on a fault line of unresolved memories and suppressed emotions. What finally brought Rajesh to seek help was not a single event but an accumulation of moments like these: a recognition that his time was dwindling, and the weight of all he'd carried for so long might soon prove too much to bear. As he sat in the waiting room of the therapist's office, fidgeting with hands worn from years of physical labor, Rajesh felt a fragile glimmer of hope. Maybe – just maybe – it wasn't too late to learn how to lay down some of this burden and rediscover the life that had been lost amidst the shadows of his memories.
